old: Manipulation often arrives with urgency, specialness, fear of missing out, threatened exclusion, sexual charge, shame, confusion, rescue fantasy, destiny, obedience, secret knowledge, or far too much certainty arriving far too quickly. You may also feel that one honest question would break the spell.
new: You are likely being manipulated if you feel any of the following; urgency, you are special, FOMO (fear of missing out), not be included, sexual charge, shame, confused, someone will rescue you, destiny, you should obey, secret knowledge, and an excessive sense of certainty about something way too quickly and you have a sense that one good question will break the spell.

old: Pause there. Don’t obey immediately, and don’t perform automatic rebellion either. Wake up inside the influence.
new: First of all, if you sense you are being hypnotically influenced, stop. Don’t obey, but don’t rebel, just realise that you are being influenced.

old: Hypnotic language turns manipulative when it smuggles in your consent, makes one choice seem inevitable, or hides a disputed claim inside the sentence.
new: Secondly, some of the ways that hypnotic language is used to manipulate are where you have consented to something you didn’t realise, or you being given only one choice, or something not yet agreed upon is embedded in a sentence. For example;

old: “When you finally admit…” “As you realize I’m right…” “The only reason you resist is…” “Part of you already knows…” “Your higher self wants…” “Everyone who is truly awake understands…” “If you doubt this, that proves your ego is afraid.”
new: You will soon realise that I am right …. Or you may, in time, decide to admit that …. Or the only reason you do not agree is …. Or part of you already knows …. Or your higher self wants …. Or everyone who is awake knows …. Or the reason you do not believe that is true is because your ego does not want you to …

old: The grammar assumes the conclusion, turns resistance into proof, and makes obedience feel like awakening.
new: If you are unsure, you may like to ask yourself the following questions;

old: “What exactly is being claimed?” “What choice is being framed as inevitable?” “What is being presupposed?” “Who benefits if I accept this frame?” “What emotion is being amplified?” “What information is missing?” “Can I say no without being punished, shamed, mocked, abandoned, or spiritually downgraded?”
new: What am I being asked to agree to? What choice am I being given? What is being assumed that I may not agree with? Who benefits if I comply? What is the emotionally charged part of what is being said? What is not being said? If I say no, what will the consequences be? (Will I be punished, shamed, laughed at, not be included, be told I am not ‘awake’ etc?)

old: A useful guide leaves the adult self more present. Powerful states need stronger boundaries.
new: This is a good guide to help engage your ‘adult’ in the conversation. The more powerful the ‘state’ the more you will need to make use of these.

old: Permissive words can still conceal coercion. I watch for the following:
new: Be aware that even when using ‘permissive’ language, you can still take away choice. Be aware of;

old: Indirect suggestion can slip past the skeptical guard because the conscious mind may never receive one clean proposition to accept or reject. The intended direction can still be quite specific even when the wording feels open, vague, conversational, or merely suggestive.
new: Indirect suggestions are a very effective way to by-pass the subject’s ‘skeptical guard’. They do this by not directly telling the subject what to do. This does not mean that indirect suggestions are not specific. It simply means that they are worded in a vague, conversational, suggestive manner.

old: Every answer means compliance: “yes,” “no,” noticing, not noticing, resistance, and silence are all redefined as proof that the suggestion is working.
new: 2) In any way making it so that whatever the subject says, shows that a suggestion has worked, when this may not be the case (this includes answering yes, no, noticing something, not noticing something, trying not to do something, not answering, etc etc etc)

old: “Whether you notice it or not” binds: uncertainty is converted into invisible success that cannot be checked.
new: 3) Including phrases such as whether or not you notice etc etc

old: Identity and ownership language: safety or goodness becomes tied to obedience, a role, the guide’s approval, or belonging to someone else.
new: 4) Including any concepts that may make a subject think they must obey, or take on a role, or that it is good/safe to please the guide or belong to someone etc etc.

old: Unannounced fractionation: moving in and out of absorption without telling you that repeated re-entry is part of the method.
new: 5) Fractionating a subject without telling them that you are going to take them in and out of absorption a few times.

old: Hidden post-session cues: words, gestures, blinks, sounds, or repeated listening are meant to produce later behavior that was not plainly disclosed.
new: 6) Giving a subject cues (words, gestures, blinks, sounds, listening a certain number of times etc) that you intend to use to make them do something at a later date, without informing them exactly what it is that they will be doing.

old: Amnesia or truth inflation: dreamlike material, missing memory, imagery, or body sensations are treated as proof of what happened.
new: 7) Including suggestions for amnesia, or making a subject think that something (dream, amnesia, imagery, body experiences etc) has happened when this may not necessarily be the case.

old: An exit that does not exit: the recording ends while preserving a role, reduced judgment, impaired movement, blankness, or an indefinite altered state.
new: 8) Not taking a subject out at the end of a recording, or leaving them with a role to play, with their judgement down, with their physical abilities down, with their minds blank, or in any other way different for an indefinite length of time.

old: A real choice includes at least one branch that doesn’t continue the induction: make it lighter, change the method, remain fully alert, pause, or stop. No remains no. Silence and uncertainty don’t become consent because the narrator has a soothing voice.
new: In order for a subject to be making a REAL choice whilst in a hypnosis, there MUST be at least one way for a subject NOT to carry on with the hypnosis if they wish. This could be by making the hypnosis lighter, using a different method of hypnosis, being in full awareness whilst in a hypnosis, or being able to pause or stop the hypnosis. Just so you know, if you say no, you are quite entitled to mean NO, even if someone with a nice voice is asking you to do something! Also, just because you don't say anything, or don't know what to say, DOES NOT mean yes!

old: Appendix C has the longer de-hypnosis checklist.
new: (see appendix C for a longer version of the de hypno)

old: An induction gathers scattered attention until quieter material becomes easier to hear. You don’t have to surrender, play asleep, or obey anyone. When you’re sober, distracted, analytical, or guarded, an actual induction may help. When meditation, loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, fatigue, or another intense opening has already made you trancey, begin with orientation and containment instead of adding depth.
Aim for the amount of trance that suits the practice: focused, warm, receptive, embodied, and still able to stop. Depth is optional.
new: Hypnotic inductions are intended to bring your attention together so that you can hear some material that you might not hear when you are sober. It is not intended as a place where you surrender yourself, or go to sleep, or need to obey anyone. Sometimes if you are sober and finding it hard to focus because you are distracted or too analytical or putting up with resistance to working on something, an induction can be useful. However if you are already pretty trancey (because you have meditated before hand, or because you are drunk on loveyhuasca or doing lucid dreaming or working on grief or listening to music or praying or tired or whatever) you might want to skip to orienting yourself and making sure you are contained before you go any further.

If you do want to induce a trance make it as deep as you need it to be for you to be able to be focussed, warm, receptive, embodied and able to stop when you need to. It doesn't have to be very deep at all.

old: Prepare the session, gather attention, deepen only when that helps, then let what you notice shape the words and the next response. Counting is one way in. Conversation, story, movement, repeated sound, and curiosity can also organize attention. Say so when you use them; elegance doesn’t excuse a covert induction.

For a simple, chosen target, you can test the suggestion before deepening. If the useful response is already happening, build from it. An induction helps you find a receptive way of listening; you don’t need to complete a ceremony before you’re allowed to respond.
new: It's preparation, gathering up your attention, sometimes it's deepening too. It will work better if you make it fit to what comes up for you. Counting is one way of gathering up your attention. You can also do it through talking, or telling a story, or movement, or sound, or encouraging you to be curious about something. If you do it through any of these means, say so. Just because it's done elegantly, doesn't mean it has to be covert.

It may be a good idea to try out the suggestion you are going to make on a simple target, to see if it works for you, before you go to the trouble of deepening. If you have already got what you want, you can always develop a more receptive response to it afterwards, you don't need all the ceremony to make it happen.

old: Choose one purpose, one starting anchor or image, and a way back. Decide whether warmth, a firm boundary, direction, or neutral witnessing would help. Floating, stairs, gardens, inner rooms, colored light, and child dialogue do not all need to report for duty at once. Switch consciously when the metaphor stops helping.

Imagery is optional. A signal may arrive through sensation, rhythm, movement, words, spatial sense, simple knowing, or no response at all. Keep the language in the world you chose: let a count mark something meaningful there, and reverse the journey when you finish. Borrow qualities such as warmth or steadiness without replacing your identity.
Pick one central verb, one sensory quality, one short refrain, and one transition phrase, then read the script aloud; long elegant sentences become soup during an induction.
new: Decide what you are going to do, and how you are going to anchor it at the beginning, and how you are going to get back. Do you want it to be warm or firm or directed or neutral or what? Don't use floating and going down stairs and going through gardens and going to inner places and seeing a colour and talking to a child inside, even if they all appeal to you! If you need to change metaphors, do it consciously.

It is OK to do this with no imagery, you will get the signal some other way. Try and make the language you use for counting in etc match the world you have chosen. Come back out again by reversing the journey in some way. It is ok to borrow qualities, but don't be somebody else.

Try and restrict yourself to one key verb, or a particular sense quality, or a small bit of text you repeat to yourself, or something, to get you from one bit to the next. Read it out loud before you start. Long beautiful sentences often turn to soup in an induction.

old: Read the induction and Come all the way back while fully awake. Choose the question or quality you want to explore, what you’re leaving alone today, and how much time you have. Love, play, confidence, creativity, and communion are worthwhile purposes; you don’t have to find a problem. Leave several minutes for returning and reflecting.

Choose a physically secure place without driving, water, machinery, or anyone needing your supervision. When intoxicated, acutely confused, or unable to keep yourself safe, deal with immediate support rather than exploratory hypnosis. The later Already open? practice is for orientation, not permission to intensify an unstable state.

Decide what kind of encouragement is welcome: spacious listening, warm company, or a firmer invitation to stay with a feeling. Preview eye closure, any repeated exit and re-entry, and the return. For a recording, read the script beforehand when possible. “Stop” ends the exercise; “less” reduces the demand; “quiet” stops the words. You can simply open your eyes and finish. No inner part has to approve your decision to stop.

When entry and return are unfamiliar, first rehearse them without a difficult subject. Once you know how to change direction, you don’t need to supervise every moment. Let a useful response become easier and less effortful. A no remains no; silence doesn’t authorize a narrator to add something you haven’t agreed to.

Let the next invitation grow from the response you got—not the response the script expected.Utilization means working with what actually happens: a thought, sound, movement, or objection may change where the practice goes. Notice what actually happens; no change doesn’t mean secret success. Keep safety and exit instructions plain. Appendix B teaches the richer language tools, and Let the next response guide you shows how to use them after the induction.
new: Before you start:

Read this induction. Come all the way back again while you are reading it. Decide what it is you want to explore, what it is you want to leave alone, how much time you have. Maybe you just want to explore having more love or play or confidence or creativity or communion or whatever, you don't have to find a problem. Make sure you have enough time to come back out again and think about it.

Make sure you are safe. Don't do this if you are driving or near water or playing with machinery or around people you need to look after. Don't do this if you are intoxicated or in any state where you might be acutely confused or unable to look after yourself - in that case you need immediate support, not exploratory hypnosis. (But see the bit above about already being open, as this is not talking about deepening when unstable).

Practise First decide on how spacious, or how firmly inviting you wish to be. Let yourself know that you will need to close your eyes, and that you may need to come out a few times, as well as coming out at the end. If you are going to record the exercise, it may be a good idea to read the script first, if possible. Remind yourself that you can always stop the exercise by saying 'stop', or 'less', or 'quiet'. Remind yourself that you can always come out simply by opening your eyes, that you do not need to get everyone's agreement inside to finish.

It is wise, until you are fully confident about coming in and out, to practise in a context where you do not need to draw on your maximum efforts. Once you know how to change direction, you will not need to supervise all the time. Your response will get easier, and less effortful. A 'no' is a 'no' and silence does not give anyone the right to add to what is not there.

You will need to develop the next part of your induction, based on what you do get. This is the principle of utilizing what you do get, and it may change what you get. If you don't get anything, then you don't get anything! Remember that you need to lay out for yourself the instructions for safety and for coming out. You will learn more about the language you can use in Appendix B. And you will learn how to use them, once the induction is over, in Let the next response guide you .

old: Read this slowly into a recorder, speak it aloud, or learn its movement and use silent words if that comes easily. Choose one anchor—a sound, bodily contact, or your two-hand practice—and an opening phrase. Keep using the same anchor where the words refer to it. Pause between paragraphs; don’t read the delivery directions aloud.
Let your eyes settle somewhere in the room, somewhere they can rest for a little while, and notice the difference between looking for something and letting what is already there come into view.

There is a surface beneath you. Notice where you meet it … the contact, the pressure, whatever you can actually feel. And while you notice that, a sound may reach you, or a breath may draw your attention, without needing you to arrange either one.
You can give this a little time.

A thought about the day may still be here. A thought about whether you’re doing this properly may be here too. There is room to notice a thought and return to the anchor you chose, without finishing the thought first.

And as you return, you may find one detail that holds your interest … something about the sound, or the contact, or that particular way of listening … and let attention stay with it long enough to become curious.

Perhaps you can give yourself the time you would give someone you care about who has begun to speak and hasn’t yet found the words. You can remain nearby, listening, without finishing their sentence for them.
Let your chosen phrase come to mind now. Say it as an invitation, and notice how it is received.
As you continue, your eyes can close, soften, or stay open. Let that be a choice you make. Listening may deepen while a sound from the room remains available in the background.
Count slowly from five to one. Give each number its own moment.

Five. Notice your chosen anchor again. Four. Let attention gather around what you find. Three. Leave a little space after the words. Two. Listen into that space, without preparing an answer. One. Stay here for a moment.
Bring your chosen concern lightly to mind, or remain with your wish for contact. Let it be present without rehearsing its whole story.
What am I noticing now?
Give the response time to take its own form. It might be a sensation, a few words, an image, a feeling, or an impulse to move. There may be nothing clear yet.
Leave room to notice, with words or without them.
new: Practise reading this slowly either into a recorder, or reading it aloud, or even learn it so that you can use it in silence. Choose to use one of the three anchors (sound, bodily contact or two hands) throughout, and use the opening phrase of your choice. Each time that 'the anchor' is mentioned in the script below, use the one that you have chosen. Pause at the end of each paragraph for a few moments. Don't read aloud the instructions to yourself about how to read it.
You might let your eyes settle somewhere in the room,
then notice the surface you are sitting (lying) on, and notice the feel of that contact, and as you notice the feel of that contact, you might notice a sound, or your own breathing,
There's all the time in the world to do this.
You may notice a thought about what has happened today, or perhaps a thought about doing this, but even if there is a thought there, you can turn your attention to the anchor,

and as you turn your attention to the anchor, you might notice something about it that interests you. Maybe it's something about the sound, or something about the contact, or even something about the way you listen,
And you might give yourself the time to notice this, just as you might give someone dear to you time to speak.
Think of a good phrase for this exercise and say it.
Feel free to close your eyes, soften them or keep them open as you go through these steps.
Count from 5 to 1, slowly.
5. Bring to mind something you want to find. 4. Focus on what you find. 3. Take a little break after the words. 2. Listen to this break. 1. Stay with it for a minute.
Bring the thing you chose to think about to mind. If you don’t want to do that, stay with the contact you made.
Now, what do you notice?
Give yourself time to notice whatever comes to you, sensations, words, images, feelings, movements etc.
Give yourself time to notice what is coming to you, whether it has words or not.

old: Use this when loveyhuasca, meditation, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, erotic energy, exhaustion, or intense beauty has already opened the state. Stabilize before making it stronger.
“The state is already open. I do not need to intensify it. I need to aim it, stabilize it, and keep it kind.”

Look around the room. Name where you are. Name the date, or at least the day. Feel your feet, hands, and spine. Press your thumbs gently but firmly against your index fingers. Focus on the physical friction of skin meeting skin.
“Only what can be integrated is welcome now. Anything too much can wait. The body may stay safe. The adult self remains present. The inner child does not have to carry this alone.”
Once you’re oriented, choose one intention:
“Please show me the next useful truth, symbol, feeling, question, or action — only in the amount I can live well with.”
new: Use this when you are already open, to contain your state.

This is good when you are already opening a state, via loveyhuasca, meditation, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, erotic energy, exhaustion, being overwhelmed by beauty, etc. You want to stabilize your state before opening it more strongly.
I already have this state open. I don’t want to open it more strongly. I want to aim it, stabilize it and keep it kind.

Look around you. Tell yourself where you are. Tell yourself the date, or at least the day. Feel your feet, hands and spine. Get a sense of yourself. Then focus on the physical sensations in your thumbs as you push them into your index fingers. Really feel the friction.
I will only allow myself to go as far as I can integrate. Too much can wait. My body will be safe. My adult self is here. My child doesn’t have to do this alone.
When you are oriented, say: “Please show me the next thing I need to know, whether it is a truth, a symbol, a feeling, a question or an action I need to take.”

old: Sit upright. Open the eyes. Feel the feet. Let the breath be natural.
Say: “I am not going away. I am coming more fully here.”
Look at one object. Feel the spine.
“Is this daydream guidance, emotional digestion, or avoidance?”
“If it is guidance, show me the action inside it. If it is avoidance, bring me gently into the present and show me what I am avoiding.”

If stillness makes you sleepy, diffuse, or escape-prone, hypnosis can become more alert rather than more relaxed. Keep the eyes open and pair a small repeated hand movement with increasing clarity; stop the movement and notice what remains without trying to disappear inward.

“Eyes open. Press thumb and forefinger together gently. Release. Again — clearer, not sleepier. One more time. Now stop the deliberate movement. Notice the first second after the rhythm ends. Is there an echo in the fingers, the breath, the attention, or nowhere at all? Stay upright and work from exactly that level of alertness.”
new: Do this sitting up, with your eyes open, feeling your feet and breathing naturally.
I am not going to go away. I am going to come here more.
Look at an object. Feel your spine.
Ask yourself if you are daydreaming to get guidance or digest emotional things, or if you are escaping.
Ask for help with whatever it is: seeing what you need to do if it is guidance, or coming into the present and seeing what you are avoiding if it is avoidance.

If you find that whenever you are still, you escape into sleepiness and diffuse states, do this exercise to increase your ability to be alert instead of relaxed. Do it with your eyes open, moving your hands. Do it for a while, and then stop it deliberately so you can see what is there without escaping.

Do this with your eyes open. Push your thumb and forefinger together gently and let go a few times, becoming more clear and alert each time. Then deliberately stop and notice what happens in the first second after you stop, whether there is an echo or not. Keep yourself up and work at this level.
Quick Inductions and Triggers: At your service.
2-hand induction:

old: Place one hand on the heart. Place the other hand on the solar plexus.
Let the heart hand represent the Nurturer. Let the solar plexus hand represent the vulnerable child.
Breathe gently.
“Love above. Child below. Adult present.”
“I send love to the child. I receive the child’s signal. I send love again. I listen again.”
new: Mind if I borrow your hands for a moment? Just for a second, put one hand on your heart, and one on your solar plexis. The one on your heart is your nurturer, the one on your solar plexis is your vulnerable child. Now just breathe gently and tell yourself, "the love is above, the child is below, and the adult is present." Tell yourself, "I will send love to the child, and I will receive the child's signal. Then I will send love again, and I will listen again."

old: Sleep induction has a different job. In inner work, the adult returns, writes, and acts. At bedtime, analysis can remain off duty. Revelation can wait; the task is rest.
For sleep hypnosis, see Nimja’s sleep playlist.
new: Sleep induction:

This induction is different, because all other inductions get you back to your adult so you can write and do stuff, and this one is going to put you to sleep so analysis can get off duty and let revelation do its thing. Try out Nimja's sleep playlist here .

old: Fractionation means returning toward ordinary awareness and then deciding whether to enter absorption again. Used openly, it teaches that trance has a door in both directions. Name the technique before using it; every answer cannot secretly mean “deeper.”

“Open the eyes and return toward ordinary awareness. Feel the room and decide whether to stop here. If you choose to continue, close or soften the eyes and notice what changes as attention gathers again. You may stop at either point.”
new: Fractionation (optional):
As long as you are open about using it, fractionation is OK.

"Open your eyes and come back, feel yourself in the room. If you want to come out of hypnosis, that's OK. But you might want to try something: close (or soften) your eyes and see if you can go back in. Remember, you can always choose to stop."
Deepening (optional):
If it is useful for you, you can go deeper into absorption. But if it isn't useful, you're already awake enough.

old: “If it is useful, attention may become more gathered. If it is not useful, I remain exactly as awake as I need to be.”
Choose one simple scene: a room in the heart, a garden, a temple, a fire with the Protector nearby, a clear lake, or a chair where the adult waits. One scene is plenty.
“Who or what needs to speak first?”
new: Take yourself to your room in your heart, your garden or temple of inner peace, sit next to a fire with your Protector, float on a lake, sit in a chair where an adult waits for you, etc, etc, etc. Just pick one.
And see who wants to talk to you first.
Trance (optional):

old: “As I wait, I give up the responsibility of making anything happen.
If it is useful, the wise subconscious may let one finger twitch, pulse, lift, warm, tingle, or become subtly noticeable when the inner meeting space is ready.
I will not force it. I will not fake it. I will simply wait with love and notice.”
new: Give yourself permission to not have to do anything.

"If it is useful, my wise subconscious may cause one of my fingers to twitch, or pulse, or lift up, or get warm, or tingly, or whatever, to let me know that I am ready to meet with whomever wants to see me in my inner space." And of course you're not going to make it happen, or pretend it is happening, you're just going to wait in love.

old: To retire the cue, stop rehearsing it, remove it from recordings or active app instructions, and return to the familiar induction. State your decision while awake; a cancellation sentence does not prove the association vanished instantly. Persistent unwanted responses or disorientation need qualified help. Any retained cue is for a future, separately chosen session; today’s altered state ends with the return.
new: And if you don't want to any more, just stop doing it, remove it from any recordings you are using, any active apps, use an induction you are familiar with and state that you are finished using it whilst awake. If this doesn't stop the association straight away, and you are still getting unwanted affects or feeling disorientated, seek qualified help to sort it out. Until the next time you want to do it, you should not use the trigger.

old: State NLP makes useful states easier to access: warmth, adult presence, courage, steadiness, love, clarity.
Strategy NLP rehearses a better response: when this cue appears, the adult does this.

Language NLP shapes the sentence: pace what is already true, open awareness, presume only safe capacity, link cause and effect carefully, embed invitations, and use de-hypnotic questions when language becomes vague, absolute, manipulative, or grandiose.
new: 2. State Level of NLP – Help them to access a new state of warmth or adult’ness or whatever
3. Strategy level of NLP – Help them to re-practice a better strategy or ‘When the cue, the adult does this’

4. Language Level of NLP – Using the language of a gentle voice which paces what is already true, opens up awareness, presumes their ability to do something safe, links events in a good cause and effect way, embeds invitations or uses de-hypnotic questions to break the effects of vague, absolutes, manipulative and grandiose language

old: The Milton Model concerns the architecture of the sentence. Commands such as “Relax now,” “Stop being anxious,” or “Trust me” often make a part brace.
Part of the point of indirect language is to get past that reflexive skeptical argument without having to overpower it. The destination can still be deliberate even when the route is subtle.
Begin with what is already true, lower the pressure, presume only a small safe capacity, and invite one movement:
“As the body notices the bed beneath it, it may become a little easier to stop holding the whole day alone.”
Pace reality. Open awareness. Validate function. Presuppose capacity. Bridge gently. Invite one small movement. Test with the body.
new: aka The Milton Model (minus the selling seminar covertly)
Have you ever had someone tell you to ‘Relax now’ or ‘Stop being anxious’ or said ‘Trust me’ and you thought to yourself NO F**KING WAY!
Well in this case we want to use ‘indirect’ language to help you get past the part that wants to argue with you and get to the place you want to be.
1. Start with what you know to be true, take the pressure off, presume what you know to be safe that they can do and invite them to do 1 thing:
2. As your body is noticing the bed beneath it, you can start to stop holding the day alone.

Here you have paced what is already real for them, opened up awareness, validated their reaction, presumed their capacity to do something, used a bridge word and invited them to do just one thing and have a way to know if it is working in their body.

old: Pacing and leading means stating what is already true before inviting anything new.
“Anxiety is here. The body is activated. A protector is trying to help. And one breath at a time, the adult can start to listen.”
The simplest form is a Truth + Invite loop:

“It is completely true that [current sensation or emotion] is here. It makes sense that my system is reacting by [current protective behavior or thought]. And right alongside that truth, my adult self is here, breathing in this room, ready to listen to whatever comes up next.”
new: Here is an example of pacing and leading when you are anxious.
It may be as simple as ‘Truth, Invite, Truth, Invite’ etc.

It is completely true that the sensation of ________ / emotion of _____ is coming up for me. It also makes sense that my system is trying to react to this by doing this/thinking ________. While that is completely true, there is another thing that is completely true and that is that my adult self is here breathing in this room right now and willing to listen to what is coming up next.

old: Awareness verbs point attention without yelling at it: notice, realize, recognize, sense, feel, wonder, imagine, picture, listen, allow, discover, remember, consider.
“Notice whether the answer comes as an image, a word, a pressure, a warmth, a silence, or a next action.”
new: ‘Awareness’ verbs: notice, realize, recognize, sense, feel, wonder, imagine, picture, listen, allow, discover, remember, consider

old: A presupposition hides an assumption inside a sentence. Use that power only to presume choice, timing, capacity, safety, love, and adult leadership. Don’t smuggle in obedience.
“Before any part has to change, it can first become more understood.”
new: Warning!!! Use this powerful tool only to presume their choice to do something when it will occur and presume their ability to do something that you know will be good for them (being in a state of safety, love, adult leading etc)

old: Words such as as, while, because, when, after, before, and which means connect one event to another. Use them carefully. A gentle voice doesn’t make a false causal claim true.
Too strong: “Because I breathe, the trauma leaves.” Better: “As I breathe, the adult self may become present enough to hear one small piece of what the wound needs.”
new: As, while, because, when, after, before, which means etc.

In general the first statement is too strong because it is unlikely that the trauma will go away just by breathing. The second statement is more accurate because as you breathe you can get your adult self present to listen to what the wounded part needs.

old: An embedded invitation places a small direction inside a larger sentence. It should invite a modest inner movement, not hide a demand.
“And somewhere inside this breath, I can let the adult self listen.”
“As I sit here, I may allow one small truth to become clear.”
“The child does not have to trust me all at once; it can simply notice I am still here.”
Use one when it helps. Ten embedded invitations in a row feel like somebody took a weekend certification.
new: Here is an example of an embedded invitation.
Example: “And as you sit there, you may allow yourself to realise…”
Another example (directed to inner child parts): “And you may allow yourself to realise that….”
I am sure you get the idea. Try using one (but don’t go overboard – if you start rattling off ten of them in a row, it becomes pretty obvious that you went on a weekend certification course, yo).

old: A manipulative double bind traps every answer inside the speaker’s agenda. An ethical one offers two genuinely safe routes.
“Would this part prefer warmth first, or space first?”
new: Maniplative double bind questions look like this:
Ethical double bind questions offer two ethically safe ways to move forward:

old: These are questions whose ordinary conversational form also acts as an invitation.
“Can the system show me the next step without showing me the whole wound?”
new: Example: “Would you rather feel a warming sensation or an expansive sensation?”
An example of using a postulate as an invitation looks like this:

old: Tag questions—isn’t it, can’t it, doesn’t it—can soften a sentence. They become oily very quickly, don’t they? Use them lightly.
“The body already knows something about resting, doesn’t it?”
new: Pattern 8: Tag questions (Is it? Cant it? Doesnt it? etc)
Works pretty much the same way as the above, but again can get a bit oily if you use it too often, so be sparing.

old: Nominalizations turn processes into nouns: healing, safety, trust, integration, communion, clarity, rest. Their vagueness can sometimes help because the subconscious supplies its own concrete meaning.
“A little more safety can arrive in whatever way the body understands.”
new: Pattern 9: Nominalisations (healing, safety, trust, integration, communion, clarity, rest etc)
Sometimes its useful to be vague about something so that the subconscious can fill in the blank with whatever will work best for them in a specific way.
Example: “And you may begin to feel more safety in whatever way is right for you.”
Pattern 10: Meta Model questions (The de-hypnosis tool)

old: The Milton Model opens possibility. The Meta Model asks exactly what somebody means. Ethical practice needs both.
“How specifically?” “According to whom?” “Compared to what?” “Always?” “Never?” “What exactly would happen?” “How do I know?” “What evidence would change my mind?”
Use Milton Model to soften into the body. Use Meta Model to return to truth.
new: To ‘Milton Model’ means to open things up, to ‘Meta Model’ means to ask “What do yo mean by that?” It is important to use both of these when working ethically with people.
“…How specifically? According to who? Compared to what? Are you saying Always? Never? What specifically will happen? How do I know? What evidence would I need to change my mind?”
So if I feel the body starting to stiffen up, I will ‘Milton’ it. If I feel I am eluding the truth, I will ‘Meta’ it.

old: Fear, craving, fantasy, belief, and memory may have sensory qualities: near or far, bright or dim, loud or quiet, moving or still, heavy or light, inside or outside the body. Work with qualities you actually notice. If none are apparent, skip this tool rather than inventing an image or voice.
Ask how the experience is represented. What changes when the image moves two feet back, the voice gets quieter, or the edge becomes less sharp?
“I am not deleting the signal. I am adjusting the volume so I can listen without being overwhelmed.”
Before moving one imaginary pixel, ask the guard whether that change is acceptable.
“Would it be okay if we moved this image back just a little, or lowered the volume slightly, purely so my adult self can stay present enough to hear what you need to tell me?”
new: Submodalities (Editing the truth without deleting it)

For this you need to have some sensory properties to work with. If the fear, craving, fantasy, belief, memory whatever, doesnt look or sound far or near, bright or dim, loud or quiet, fast or slow, inside or outside the body, heavy or light etc, then just dont use this tool.
“How is this represented, and how can I change its properties in a way that will serve me better?”
“I’m not deleting this signal, I’m just altering the volume so that I can hear it without being overwhelmed.”
(If you have a guard, its a good idea to ask them first if it’s ok to do this)
“Is it ok if I move the image a bit further away, or turn the volume of the voice down so that my adult self can be here and hear what you need to say to me?”
Anchoring (The back to hypnosis doorway)

old: An anchor is a cue connected to a state: a hand on the heart, two fingers touching, a breath, a word, a posture, scent, or song. Find a real state you want easier access to, feel it, and pair the cue while it is clearly present with the phrase, “This is available.” For hypnotic re-entry, choose a usable receptive state rather than peak emotional intensity; follow “A shortcut back into hypnosis” in the main induction section. Keep alert calming and the synchronicity wake-up cue separate.
new: There are many ways to do this. Put your hand on your heart, touch two fingers together, use a breath, a word, a particular body posture, smell, song, whatever. Feel something that you have got to in reality that you want to be able to get to easily when you need to. Do your anchor thing and say to yourself that this is available to you. Do make sure you do it when you have clearly got it. To get yourself back into a good hypnosis state easily, dont go for a peak state but for a good hypnotic state. See the main induction for a quick way to get back into hypnosis. Do make sure this is different from both your alert and calm cue and your synchronicity wake up cue.

old: People notice a synchronicity and immediately ask what it means. Sometimes that opens insight; sometimes it starts compulsive pattern-hunting. I prefer using the moment of noticing as a wake-up bell. The coincidence doesn’t have to contain a message. It has already captured attention, which is enough.
The cue I give myself is:

“Whenever I notice something that feels like a synchronicity, I wake up inside the state I am in. I feel my body and the room. I remember that the coincidence is not proof of an interpretation. I let attention widen beyond the story my current mood is telling. I ask what is fact, what is interpretation, what needs warmth, what needs protection, and what needs action. I return to the highest perspective I can access without leaving the body, the facts, or ordinary human reality.”
I make room for whatever is genuinely available: objectivity, clarity, ease, peace, freedom, joy, and gratitude. I do not have to manufacture any of them.
Synchronicity noticed → pause → orient → widen → reality-test → listen → choose one loving action.

The cue interrupts identification without erasing the state’s message. A negative state may still contain an inner-child need, a Protector warning, grief, a bodily problem, or a real demand for action.
new: Using synchronicity (The synchronicity wake up cue)

People often ask what the synchronicity means. Sometimes they get a great insight from it, but other times they get obsessed trying to work out patterns etc. I am using the noticing of the synchronicity to WAKE UP.
It is my cue to:

Whenever I notice it I use it as a cue for waking up from whatever state I am in, feeling my body, feeling the room I'm in, remembering that what I'm noticing is not proof for what I'm interpreting from the coincidences, widening my state so that I can see beyond what my current state is showing me. I then look for the truth of what is going on (What is really going on, what is just my interpretation? What needs to be warmed? What needs to be protected? What action needs to be taken?) and I go into the highest state I can get into where I can objectively and clearly see what is going on from that situation from the highest perspective I can get to, whilst remaining in my body, not leaving the facts of the situation and not leaving my regular human state. From that state I feel my feelings. I look for the truth of the situation. If I am in a negative state, I check if it is a message from my Inner Child, my Protector or if I just need to grieve. I check if it is a message from my physical body (if there is a problem with my body that needs to be taken care of) or if there is something that needs to be done about the situation. From that place I choose what to do. I choose at least one thing to do that is from a loving place. I allow myself to be in whatever state is real for me, which now includes objectivity, clarity, ease, peace, freedom, joy, gratitude, etc.
In other words: Stop-orient-go wider-reality check-listen-do at least one thing from a loving place.
This way I don't go into identification but I still hear the message of the state if it's negative.

old: Imagine noticing an ordinary, harmless synchronicity.
Feel the moment when attention says, “Whoa.”
Use that opening to feel the feet, body, breath, and room.
Repeat: “The noticing is my wake-up bell, not proof of a message.”
Ask the Nurturer, Protector, and Leader what each sees.
Rehearse returning to a grounded, wider perspective.
End with one small action and the complete waking exit.
The cue remains self-authored, visible, reversible, and limited to orientation. It can’t authorize a decision, prove an intuition, suppress a warning, or let another person control the response.

Psychologically, this resembles an implementation intention: an advance “if X, then Y” plan that links a recognizable cue with a chosen response. Gollwitzer’s foundational paper supports the general mechanism. This particular use of synchronicity hasn’t been studied directly.

The same mechanism creates the risk: rehearsing synchronicity as a cue may make you scan for it. Pattern perception can drift toward false-positive meaning, especially during absorption or destabilization. Research links stronger apophenic pattern detection with false-positive judgments and psychosis-spectrum traits, although ordinary pattern noticing is not itself pathological. See Blain and colleagues and Grant and colleagues.

Deactivate the cue if it increases compulsive scanning, sleeplessness, anxiety, certainty that random events are personally directed messages, or difficulty distinguishing observation from interpretation.

To retire it, stop rehearsing it and say while fully awake: “Synchronicity is no longer a cue. I release this association and return coincidence to ordinary uncertainty.” Remove it from the written cue list and stop rehearsing it. The statement expresses your decision; it does not prove the association has vanished immediately.
new: How to install Synchronicity cues:
Mentally rehearse the following: Imagine that you have noticed a synchronicity that is obviously harmless.
Feel the "whoa" of stimulation that you just got from noticing it.
Use that stimulation to feel your feet, your body, your breathing, your room.
Reiterate to yourself that whenever you notice a synchronicity, it is just a bell that rings to wake you up, it is not proof for what you are interpreting from it.
Ask yourself: "What does my Nurturer think about this?", "What does my Protector think about this?", "What does my Leader think about this?"
Rehearse going back to a more grounded state and to a more wide view of the situation.
Rehearse yourself taking at least one action. Rehearse yourself waking up completely.

Mind the caveats! You must be the one authoring these. You must see them. You can always undo them. You must use them only to help you orient. They do not authorize you to make a decision. They are not proof for what your intuition is telling you. They do not stop you from hearing the message of your intuition if it is warning you about something. You can't use them to control other people.

This is very similar to implementation intention . I'm not aware of research into implementation intention for this specific thing, but the general mechanisms appear to work; a paper explaining how and why they work can be found here .

A downside of synchronicity cues is that they can lead to false positives. We do this on purpose when we rehearse what to do when we notice a synchronicity (we create an association in our head); however, when you are absorbed in something and/or when you are destabilized, you might think that you saw a synchronicity when in fact there wasn't any. Research has shown that people that score high on apophenia tests also score high for detecting patterns that were not really there, as well as scoring high on psychosis spectrum traits [1, 2] (this is not saying that noticing patterns is bad; in fact, it's not a pathology).

If you feel that synchronicity cues are making these things worse (e.g. you feel like you have to look for them all the time, you can't sleep, you feel anxious, you are sure that random things happen in your life in order to tell you something, you can't tell the difference between noticing something and interpreting what it might mean, etc.), you should deactivate synchronicity cues.

You can do that by not rehearsing them anymore and by saying to yourself (when you are fully awake) that you don't want to use synchronicity as a cue anymore (e.g. "From now on, I am no longer going to use noticing synchronicity as a cue for waking up."). Remove it from your list of cues, so that you won't rehearse it anymore.

old: Dishonest reframing declares that the problem was secretly good all along. I prefer questions that widen meaning without lying:
“What else might be true?” “What is this part trying to do for me?” “What would the Nurturer, the Protector, and the Leader each say about this?”
new: In the past I used to reframe by telling myself that whatever problem I had was actually a good thing. However, that is not honest. Now I reframe by asking myself:

old: First: what do I feel from inside myself? Second: if I sit inside the other person, what might they be feeling or protecting? Third: if I watched this from across the room, what would I notice? Fourth: from the universal heart, what serves truth, love, boundaries, and the good of everyone involved?
Don’t use perceptual positions to excuse harm. Use them to escape the prison of one angle.
new: Here is a rough outline of the NLP tools and techniques I use:
Perceptual Positions : 1) seeing from Self, 2) then seeing from Other, 3) then seeing from Witness, and 4) then seeing from Universal Heart. I do this to see the situation with more accuracy.
I will not use this to rationalize bad behavior, but only to break out of a prison of perception.

old: Don’t end with “I understand.” Ask where life will test the understanding, picture the actual cue, and rehearse the smallest better response.
“If [cue], then I [small action].”
new: Future Pacing : 1) Once I have seen the situation more clearly, I will imagine future scenarios where my old behavior would have triggered, to test out if my new insight is working.
If these scenarios come up, I will choose new small behaviors using an Implementation Intention (If...then... statement)

old: Classic NLP uses the Swish to replace an old self-image with a new one. Done mechanically, it can feel like an inner eviction. Here, the old pattern stays visible, the new possibility stands beside it, and I notice the body’s response while comparing what each future would actually require.
new: Swish Variation : 2) I use an NLP technique called a "Swish Pattern", but I will allow my old pattern to be there, while also holding my new pattern in my awareness. I feel what comes up somatically, and compare the differences between the future scenarios of my old and new patterns.

old: “What does one side want?” “What does the other side fear?” “What need sits under both?” “What third option honors both without letting either run the whole life?”
new: Parts Integration : I use this technique to ask my conflicting parts what they want, what they are afraid of, what their need is, and see if I can find a 3rd option that satisfies both parts needs, without either part dominating my behavior.

new: Here is a list of things I do not do with NLP :
I do not deny people's legitimate signals.
I do not tell people to override their fear.
I do not use NLP for memory retrieval.
I do not use NLP to manipulate other people or convince myself of my intuition.
I do not remove legitimate signals or medical symptoms.
I do not use NLP on people who are panicked, destabilized, manic, having a "psychosis-like state", or are too high/dissociated to reality test.
I do not use NLP to make people feel like they are spiritually inferior to me if they disagree with me.
I do not use covert commands in my language.
I do not use NLP with people when there isn't enough time (I create urgency for them).
I do not use NLP on people without their consent (the idea that "your subconscious will let me know if you want me to do this" is NOT consent).
I do not use NLP on people in a suggestible state (in trance, tired, attracted to me, feeling shame or grief, or chemically altered).
Here is a rough outline of the entire NLP process (though I rarely do all of this) :

old: Induce or contain. Gather attention, or stabilize first if you are already wide open.
Ask permission. Is it useful to work with this image, feeling, or pattern today?
Represent the pattern. How does this show up — image, voice, sensation, posture, distance, size, color, movement?
Ask what it protects. What is this trying to do for me?
Adjust the form, gently. Move it back, lower the volume, add space, change posture, slow the scene.
Bring in the three adults. Nurturer warms, Protector makes it safe, Leader points a direction.
Anchor the useful state. Heart, fingers, breath, posture.
Future pace. If the old cue shows up, what is the smallest new action?
Check the fit and the evidence. What changes in the body? Is the response kind and doable? What supports the interpretation beyond how it feels?
Exit and act. Come back to the room. Do one ordinary thing.
new: Induce/Contain the person (get their attention or stabilize them).
Ask for their permission.
Get a representation of their pattern (image, feeling, size, color, location, movement, etc.).
Find out what that part/pattern is protecting for them.
Change some aspect of their pattern (location, volume, space, posture, speed, etc.).
Put 3 good adults in with the person (Nurturer, Protector, and Leader).
Anchor the person's good state (heart, fingers, breath, posture, etc.).
Future pace a scenario for them where their old pattern would have triggered, and have them do a small new behavior (If...then... statement).
Have them check in with their body for changes and look for evidence to support their new interpretation of the situation.
Get the person out of the altered state (bring them back to the room and have them do something).

old: I’m speaking from experience in this appendix.

During self-hypnosis, meditation, lucid dreaming, loveyhuasca, grief, prayer, plant-medicine-adjacent practice, or other altered states, people sometimes meet something that doesn’t feel like an ordinary emotion or younger part. It may appear as a demon, jinn, parasitic energy, dark intelligence, or terrifying archetype—a voice or image that feels intrusive, hateful, seductive, mocking, or simply alien.

I don’t need this guide to settle the metaphysics. Perhaps these are literal beings. Perhaps they are symbolic mind-forms, trauma in a frightening costume, dissociated energy, or ancestral and relational burdens. The practical question is:
“What response makes me safer, clearer, more loving, more grounded, and less hooked?”
new: I speak here from experience.

When you’re doing hypnosis, meditation, lucid dreaming, loveyhuasca-ing, going through a period of intense grief, praying, or whatever else may alter your consciousness, it’s possible you may run into something that you perceive to be a demon, a jinn, a parasitic energy, or whatever other dark entity or terrifying archetype you may encounter – it may be a voice or an image, and it does n’t just feel like an emotion or a younger part of you, but something that feels intrusive, hateful, seductive, mocking, etc.

First of all, it doesn’t matter if they’re demons or not. They may be literal demons, for all you know. Or they may be manifestations of your mind, burdens you’re carrying from previous relationships, whatever. What matters is what is the best way to deal with them.

old: When a demonic, jinn-like, hostile, or intrusive presence appears, don’t reward it with instant metaphysical certainty. Run the triage first: medical danger, environment, body, overload, and how open the mind has become. Open the eyes, feel the feet, name the room, lower stimulation, leave hostile company, and stop adding prompts. Don’t deepen, hunt for hidden truth, or debate ontology while destabilized.
“Only what can be integrated is welcome now. Anything too much can wait. The adult self remains present. The body may return to safety.”

Danger to self or others, psychosis-like fear, inability to sleep, extreme paranoia, chest pain, seizures, serious overheating, overdose concern, or loss of basic functioning means the self-hypnosis session is over. Get real-world help.
new: So what do you do when you encounter a demon, or a jinn, or something else that’s bad and intrusive?

First of all, do the usual things – make sure you’re not in danger from a medical standpoint, check your environment, check your body, make sure you’re not overstimulating yourself, make sure you’re not opening your mind too much. If you need to, open your eyes, ground yourself in your body and your environment, remove yourself from any bad influence you’re surrounding yourself with, stop stimulating your mind. Don’t go further into whatever it is you’re doing – don’t be curious, don’t try to figure out what it is.
Tell yourself, “If this can be integrated in this moment, it’s welcome. If not, it can wait until later. The adult part of me is always welcome, and so is my body.”

If you feel like you’re in any danger of doing anything harmful to yourself or others, if you feel like you’re going psychotic and you’re afraid of it, if you feel like you won’t be able to sleep when the self-hypnosis session is over, if you feel overly paranoid, if you feel physical pain in your chest, if you feel like you’re going to have a seizure, if you feel like you’re too hot in a bad way, if you feel like you’ve taken too much of something, if you feel like you won’t be able to function in the world anymore – then the self-hypnosis session is over, and you should get help in the “real world”.

old: Once you’re stable enough to stay present, notice what helps without turning the response into a metaphysical test. Put a hand on the heart if that feels welcome, take a comfortable breath, and keep the room available.
I don’t have to decide what this is right now. I can notice whether warmth or distance helps, and keep my boundary either way. Nothing here requires my obedience.

If vulnerability appears—a knot in the throat, sadness, fear, or a sense of trying to protect something—you can bring in the Nurturer. If the experience remains hostile or becomes more frightening, stop engaging with it and return to the body and room.

Neither response establishes its origin. A protective part needn’t reveal its fear quickly; a comforting response doesn’t prove an interpretation either. The useful question is whether this way of responding helps you become clearer, steadier, and less hooked. Love and boundaries don’t require a verdict first.
new: If, however, you feel like you can deal with it, check in with yourself and see what’s best to do. Again, it doesn’t matter if it’s a demon or not. Put your hand on your heart, breathe comfortably, and check in with yourself about what to do in this situation.
Internalize the fact that you don’t have to know what it is. Find out if it helps to be warm towards it or to keep it at arm’s length. Keep in mind that you don’t have to do what it tells you to do.

If you feel vulnerable, if you feel tightness in your throat, if you feel sadness or fear or a need to protect yourself from it, call upon your Nurturer. If you don’t feel better, or if it continues being hostile towards you, stop trying to deal with it.

Internalize the fact that you don’t have to know where it comes from. Check in with yourself about whether or not this is helpful. You don’t have to find out if it’s a protector immediately, and you may not be able to comfort it quickly, but work with it as if it were, at least for now.

old: The first impulse may be to fight, banish, hate, prove power, argue, panic, or identify completely with the threatened self. Some traditions use prayers, mantras, protections, banishing rituals, or exorcism forms, and some people find them useful. But fighting from fear can fasten attention more tightly to the thing you want gone.
Fear gives it center stage. Hatred gives it a hook. Pride gives it an opponent. Panic gives it the nervous system.
“I do not need to hate this. I do not need to merge with this. I do not need to obey this. I do not need to defeat this from fear. I return to loving awareness.”
new: Your first instinct may be to fight it, banish it, hate it, show it that you’re more powerful than it is, argue with it, panic, become your own lesser self in fear of it, etc. Some people may want to use traditional prayer or mantras or protection or banishing or exorcism techniques, and those may well work for them. But if you’re fighting it out of fear…
It only becomes a center of attention if you hate it and therefore give it a hook in you. (To counter pride, or to feel you must panic and defeat it.)

So the next time it comes up you can just say, “I see that there is no reason to hate and revile what I am experiencing. I see that there is no reason to merge with or become what I am experiencing. I see that there is no reason to obey what I am experiencing. I see that there is no reason to try to defeat what I am experiencing out of fear. I choose to return my attention to loving awareness.”

old: When the presence feels hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, or boundary-violating, don’t offer soft sentimental love as though inviting it in for tea. Use love with a boundary.

Sit upright. Press your feet into the floor. Let the spine rise. Gently draw the shoulder blades back so the chest is open but not exposed. Feel the skin boundary of the torso. Feel that this body has a perimeter.

“I recognize that suffering may be here, and I wish all suffering to return to the space where it belongs. But the boundary of this skin belongs to my adult life. You do not have permission to enter this house.”
“Compassion is present. The door is closed.”
new: This is especially important if the presence feels in any way hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, etc – if it doesn’t feel like it respects your boundaries. You don’t want to approach it with soft sentimental love in this case; you want to approach it with love but also maintain a boundary.

So, sit up, get grounded in your feet, straighten your spine, pull your shoulder blades back just slightly so that your chest is open but not exposed, feel the boundary of your skin all around your torso, feel the perimeter of your body, and simply say, “While I recognize that there may be suffering present here, I want all suffering to go back where it came from. The boundary of this skin is the boundary of an adult now. You don’t get to come in the house anymore.”

old: A symbolic hostile-presence experience that settles with grounding and love is very different from a state that becomes persistent, paranoid, sleepless, dangerous, or impossible to reality-test.

If somebody believes they’re under attack for days, can’t sleep or function, hears commands, feels compelled to hurt themselves or anyone else, becomes manic, can’t communicate normally, or can’t distinguish symbolic experience from ordinary reality, stop treating the problem as hypnosis material. Get help.

If the practice makes you more loving, grounded, relational, honest, and functional, continue gently. If it makes you more paranoid, sleepless, grandiose, isolated, frightened, or unreal, stop deepening and get support.
new: This is assuming that you are having a symbolic experience of “hostile presences” which responds to grounding and love. It may be that what you are experiencing is actually psychotic or a form of destabilization.

If you feel like you are under attack for multiple days at a time, if you are not able to sleep, if you are not able to function normally, if you are hearing voices telling you to do things, if you feel you need to hurt yourself or somebody else, if you feel you are going manic, if you feel you can’t communicate normally, if you feel you can’t distinguish between what you are experiencing symbolically and normal reality, get help immediately. It’s not something to deal with in hypnosis.

As a general rule, if this is making you more loving, more grounded, more relational, more honest, and more functional, then it’s probably OK to keep doing it gently. If it’s making you more Paranoid, more sleepless, more grandiose, more isolated, more scared, or more unreal, don’t go deeper, get help.

old: Hostile presences, shadow forces, grandiose parts, and altered-state imagery don’t always attack through fear. Sometimes they seduce through importance: a cosmic secret, a special mission, a vast download, a feeling of being uniquely chosen, or a revelation that makes washing dishes seem beneath your new rank.

“Thank you for the imagery. I do not require a grand performance. If this information cannot become a simple, honest act of care tomorrow morning — washing the dishes, cleaning my room, keeping a promise, apologizing, resting, eating, or helping someone I love — it is not useful to my path.”
Guidance worth keeping should make ordinary life more beautiful, honest, relational, humble, reliable, and useful to other people.
new: Finally, presences, shadow forces, or grandiose parts may try to respond by giving you a sense that you’re special, trying to “download cosmic info” to you, try to give you a special mission, make you feel doing the dishes is beneath you, etc. You can just say, “Thank you for the imagery, but I don’t need your grand performance. Unless the info you’re trying to download to me can help me do the dishes, clean my room, be more honest, be more helpful, be more loving, keep my promises, take care of my body by resting and eating etc. I don’t need it.
Unless the “guidance” you’re trying to give me can help me be more beautiful, honest, relational, humble, useful, and take care of my dishes and my room, I don’t need it.”

old: Demons, jinn, hostile presences, and “Unattached Burdens” all lead to the same practical training: can love remain present without surrendering the boundary, and can the mind become harder to hook? I’m not trying to turn anyone into an entity hobbyist.
new: Finally, some of you may be tempted to make this an area of hobbyism – to become interested in demons or jinns or hostile presences or Unattached Burdens or whatever. I just don’t want you to do that. They all lead to the same thing, which is how to maintain a presence of love while also making your mind harder to hook. Beyond that, I don’t want you to be hobbyists in this area.

old: Preview the sequence, choose one purpose, and decide whether you want to begin. Each family can be light, eyes-open, or replaced by no-trance contact. Notice the actual response—including no change—and let it determine the next move. Move, imagine, change the sensory channel, remain still, or stop. Use the complete waking return after every induction.
If vivid images don’t come, translate the metaphor into words, rhythm, spatial sense, touch, movement, or simple knowing. The mind doesn’t owe anybody a movie.
new: Practise! Work out in advance which one you want to do and what you want to use it for (pick just one) and whether or not you want to do it at all! Any of these ‘families’ of induction can be done as light inductions, with eyes open, or instead of trance you can just do them as a contact. Once you start an induction, you will want to notice what’s going on (even if nothing changes) and work out what to do next, move, imagine something else, change the sensory channel you’re using, do nothing, stop the induction sequence and do something else… . Whatever you do, make sure you bring yourself back to waking at the end of an induction.
NB: if you can’t ‘see’ the images you’re trying to visualise, that’s fine, change them into words, rhythm, spatial relations, something to touch or move or just plain ‘knowing’… .

old: Feel the support beneath you and the position of one hand or foot. Press gently, stretch slightly, and release—or imagine it. Notice ease, tension, warmth, breath, or no change. Repeat with no more than three areas, letting “release” guide the sequence. Which area or inner voice wants attention? What support is needed? Restore ordinary movement and return.
new: Stretch and Release: Work out what will be supporting you, focus on the feeling of support. You can also focus on where one of your hands or feet is. Either actually, or in your imagination, stretch a little bit, either stretching that part of your body slightly or pressing down into the support, and then let go of the effort, just relax. See if there is any difference, even if there isn’t. Do this for no more than 3 places on your body. Think of it as ‘releasing’ as you go through the sequence. Which bit of your body, or voice, needs this? What do you need to support it? Bring your body back to normal movement and return.

old: Notice where your weight is carried. Let support carry 1% more effort, as if floating without losing contact, or keep ordinary weight and pressure. Notice the response. You may deliberately alternate attention toward ordinary awareness on the inhale and support on the exhale; name this fractionation beforehand. What becomes easier to hear? Keep the support, regain chosen weight and firm contact, then return.
new: Supported Floating: Work out what is supporting you and where your weight is, imagine that the support is holding a tiny bit (1%) more of your effort. It’s like floating but you don’t have to lose contact, or just keep it at the same level, just enough weight/pressure. See what happens, you can fractionate this if you want, perhaps noticing your normal awareness when you breathe in and the support when you breathe out. Tell yourself you are going to do this before you do it. What can you hear more easily now? Bring yourself back to normal feeling of support and return.

old: Accompany a natural rhythm: breath, a comfortable hum, a finger tap, outside sound, or silent counting. No rhythm is also an option. Repeat “here, and here again,” noticing where attention lands between repetitions. Stop the deliberate rhythm and notice the first quiet beat, without trying to become blank. Is a word, feeling, need, or action clearer? Let ordinary rhythm resume and return.
new: Rhythmic: Use your breathing or slightly hum in your throat to make a natural rhythm, or tap your finger or listen to sounds outside to make an artificial one. You can even do it by counting to yourself (silently) or with no rhythm at all. Tell yourself you are going to say “here, and here again” over and over, and notice what you pay attention to in between the phrases, then stop saying it. Notice what you become aware of in the first beat – you don’t need to make your mind blank, just notice what comes up. Does it make any words, feelings, needs or actions more clear? Bring back your normal rhythm and return.

old: Notice a concern with several strands. Imagine yarn unwinding, bubbles settling, or knots placed visibly beside you. Leave the object unchanged or label it in words when that fits better. Count only strands you actually set down; nothing is erased. Which needs warmth, protection, or action? Keep one useful strand, give the others a visible holding place, and return.
new: Unwinding Object: Good for when you have a few different strands to one thing you want to work on. Imagine an object unwinding – maybe some yarn, some bubbles, or some knots that you place beside you. Once you’ve placed them all, give yourself a minute to look at them all, you don’t have to change anything, but you can label them if you need to (just a word or two). How many did you put down? Which one do you need to work on, what does it need – warmth, protection, action? Keep one strand in your attention and put the others somewhere you can see them and return.

old: Hear the actual room and feel the body before imagining a step toward a chosen destination. Use footsteps, textures, or landmarks to gather attention. Change scenery or skip directly to dialogue when useful. Notice a detail without assigning hidden meaning; the mystery is how the scene develops, not what will be done to you. Who or what needs to speak? Return by the same route and close the imagined space.
new: Sensory Journey: Pay attention to the sounds in the room you’re in and how your body feels, then imagine yourself walking somewhere. Where do you want to go? Listen to the sounds of your footsteps and take in your surroundings as you walk, what do objects feel like if you touch them, what landmarks do you see? When you feel you have enough of your attention, imagine the scenery changing until you are in a place where you can talk to whoever you need to (or you can just cut to the chase, if you prefer). Pay attention to something without worrying about what it means. Allow yourself to be curious about what’s going to happen next, but don’t make it a “what are they going to do to you?” kind of thing. When you are ready to finish, imagine yourself walking back the way you came and close the space.

old: Start with a small neutral area and what is already there. Imagine warmth, steadiness, or attention spreading to the next comfortable area, or keep it localized. Pause at each step and notice what changes without claiming medical repair. Does the body want contact, space, words, or ordinary care? Let the image recede, feel the whole body and real contact points, and return.
new: Gradual wave: start with a very small neutral area, feel into it a little and then imagine a wave spreading out to a new area that is still ok. Sense into the new area (or continue using the old). See if there is anything that could use medical attention, and if you imagine it being fixed, what is different afterwards? Does the body want any contact, space, words, other care? Let the mental image go, sense your body, sense your contact points, come back.

old: Prepare time, a place, tools, and boundaries for patient care. Let a signal, feeling, or younger state approach only as closely as welcome; choose language that doesn’t make you feel fragmented. Ask before responding, wait, reconnect only where welcome, rest, and reassess. An available inner adult or one borrowed function can help; you choose words, pace, and action. Aim for “good as you,” not erased history. Close the workspace, affirm wholeness and adult presence, and return.
new: Care workshop: prepare the workshop (time, place, tools, boundaries, etc). Invite the signal/feeling/young part to come as close as they want. Try to avoid any language that makes you not one person. Care for it as best you can, by asking what it wants and giving that if you can, or sensing into it and responding, or just being with it. Take breaks, get back in contact if that's ok, take more breaks, etc. Keep bringing in adult functions (or borrow someone else's function). Have the adult part of you run the show. Goal is to make it "good as you". Close the workspace, reassure yourself that you are one whole person, that you're an adult now, and come back.

old: Choose qualities you understand: warmth, boundary, steadiness, curiosity, or dignity. Imagine posture, voice, or attention with 1% more access to one quality. Observe rather than embody it when preferred. Notice a movement, word, image, or no response. Repeat to strengthen access, not replace identity. How would that quality meet today’s situation? Keep the quality and one useful action, release the role, affirm “I am myself,” and return.
new: Resource: pick a resource quality. Imagine yourself accessing 1% more of that quality (or just sense yourself). What is different? How is your body, voice, etc? Do this a few times to strengthen it. Come back, keeping the quality and one positive action that you would do with it, but leaving the "person" behind, saying "I am me".

old: Observable pacing: Keep the eyes open, name the room and day, feel the feet, and read or write in ordinary awareness. Invitation: Ask one clear question and wait without narrowing attention further. Genuine choice: Answer, write “unsure,” rest, change the question, seek another person’s view, or stop. Autonomous signal: Record a word, sensation, impulse, objection, or silence without interpreting it as proof. Deepener: None. Full alertness is not an inferior version of the practice. Handoff: Let the internal adult respond in writing or through one practical choice. Integration and exit: Reality-test the signal and do one small action. Because no altered state was cultivated, simply close the exercise and continue the day.
new: For the no trance inner contact, I would do: Pacing: notice you can see, it's (day of the week), you have feet, you can read, you can write, etc. Suggestion: in your mind, ask a question, but don't focus too hard. Choice: you can answer the question, write an answer, write that you don't know, take a break, rephrase the question, ask someone else, stop doing this, etc. Autonomous: write whatever you get. Deepener: none. Handoff: have your adult self answer the question in whatever way is appropriate, preferably by writing or doing. Integration/exit: reality test the autonomous, do something based on it, stop doing it.
